header:
Problem 3 Pinene in Polymers
Pinene is extracted from pine oil and is an important class of natural products with broad applications in synthetic polymers.

subquestions.text_open: 3.1 Cationic polymerization of \beta-pinene can produce a high-molecular-weight polymer used in optoelectronic materials. A \beta-pinene-based polymer synthesis is shown below. 3.1.1 Polymers A and B are known not to contain bridged rings. Write the SMILES structures of polymers A and B, explicitly including the end groups. For each polymer, provide three structures: (a) the repeat unit, using '[X]' and '[Y]' at connections to other repeat units or end groups; (b) the '[X]' end group, using * at the connection to the polymer backbone; and (c) the '[Y]' end group, using * at the connection to the polymer backbone.

text_images.description: Reaction scheme for 3.1: molecule 'CC1(C)[C@@H]2C(CC[C@H]1C2)=C', labeled "\beta-Pinene" below, reacts with molecule 'CC(Cl)(C)C1=CC=CC=C1' under `EtAlCl_2` to form **A**. **A** then reacts further under `H_2, Pd/Al_2O_3` to give **B**.

subquestions.text_open: 3.1.2 If a polymer chain bearing pinene, or a derivative thereof, at both ends is desired, state how the preceding reaction should be modified.

3.2 \alpha-Pinene (structure shown below) is a biologically renewable feedstock. \alpha-Pinene itself is difficult to polymerize into a polymer by radical polymerization, but the unsaturated ketone obtained by selective oxidation of \alpha-pinene (structure shown below) can undergo conventional radical polymerization to give a high-molecular-weight polymer. 3.2.1 From the perspective of monomer structure, explain the difference in radical-polymerization reactivity between \alpha-pinene and the unsaturated ketone.

text_images.description: The image shows two chemical structures. On the left is 'CC1(C)[C@@H]2C(C)=CC[C@H]1C2', labeled "\alpha-Pinene" below. On the right is 'CC([C@H](C3)C4)(C)[C@@H]3C(C4=O)=C', labeled "pinocarvone" below.

subquestions.text_open: 3.2.2 Structural characterization shows that the backbone of the polymer obtained from the unsaturated ketone contains two different repeat-unit structures. Write the SMILES structures of both repeat units, using an asterisk (*) for the connection sites between repeat units.
